hints: Focus on what makes ethane different from ethene, think single bond versus double bond and tetrahedral versus planar.
Recall that ethane is $\text{C}_2\text{H}_6$ with only single bonds and tetrahedral $109^\circ$ angles, while ethene is $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ with a C=C double bond and planar $120^\circ$ angles.
Remember that every single and double covalent bond contains one $\sigma$ bond, but only a double bond adds a $\pi$ bond, so ask which bond type must appear in both.
walkthrough:
**Draw the two molecules in your mind**

Think like a teacher with models. Ethane is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_3$ with a C-C single bond. Ethene is $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2$ with a C=C double bond.

$$\text{ethane: } \text{C}_2\text{H}_6 \text{ (alkane, single bonds only)}$$ $$\text{ethene: } \text{C}_2\text{H}_4 \text{ (alkene, one C=C double bond)}$$

**Compare shape and bond angle**

Ethane carbons are tetrahedral with angles about $109^\circ$ and the molecule is 3D, not flat. Ethene carbons are trigonal planar with angles about $120^\circ$ and the molecule is flat.

$$\text{ethane: tetrahedral, } \approx 109^\circ, \text{ non-planar}$$ $$\text{ethene: trigonal planar, } \approx 120^\circ, \text{ planar}$$

**Compare sigma and pi bonding**

Here is the key rule to remember. Every covalent bond has one $\sigma$ bond. A double bond is one $\sigma$ plus one $\pi$.

$$\text{single bond = 1 } \sigma$$ $$\text{double bond = 1 } \sigma + 1 \pi$$
So both ethane and ethene must contain $\sigma$ bonds, but only ethene contains a $\pi$ bond.

options.A: Incorrect. Only ethene is planar because its C=C double bond prevents rotation and holds all six atoms in one plane. Ethane has tetrahedral carbons with free rotation about the C-C single bond, so it is 3D, not planar.
options.B: Incorrect. Bond angles of about $109^\circ$ are tetrahedral and apply only to ethane. Ethene has trigonal planar carbons with bond angles of about $120^\circ$.
options.C: Correct. Both molecules contain $\sigma$ covalent bonds. In fact, all C-H bonds are $\sigma$ bonds, the C-C single bond in ethane is $\sigma$, and the C=C double bond in ethene also contains one $\sigma$ bond (plus one $\pi$).
options.D: Incorrect. Only ethene has a $\pi$ covalent bond, from the second bond in the C=C double bond. Ethane has only single bonds, so it has $\sigma$ bonds only and no $\pi$ bonds.
